overview: Einiosaurus procurvicornis ("buffalo lizard") was a centrosaurine ceratopsid from the Two Medicine Formation of Montana (~74 Ma), immediately recognisable by its strongly downward-curved nasal horn — unique among ceratopsids — and two long spikes projecting upward from the top of the frill. It represents part of a remarkable stratigraphic succession of centrosaurines through the Two Medicine Formation, where different species appear in successive layers.

Massive bone beds preserve hundreds of Einiosaurus individuals — consistent with herding behaviour and catastrophic mass mortality events comparable to those in Alberta. The Two Medicine centrosaurine succession (Rubeosaurus → Einiosaurus → Achelousaurus) shows an apparent anagenetic or cladogenetic sequence of forms through time, providing one of the best records of ceratopsid evolution within a single formation.

articles.title: Discovery
articles.body: Scott Sampson described Einiosaurus procurvicornis in 1995 from Two Medicine Formation material. The downward-curved nasal horn is the most diagnostic feature and gives the animal an immediately distinctive profile among ceratopsids. Bone beds with hundreds of individuals confirm its social, herding lifestyle.

articles.title: Two Medicine succession
articles.body: Three centrosaurine species appear in successive stratigraphic levels of the Two Medicine Formation over ~2.5 million years: Rubeosaurus ovatus (oldest), Einiosaurus procurvicornis (intermediate) and Achelousaurus horneri (youngest). Whether this represents true evolutionary succession within a single evolving lineage (anagenesis) or replacement by separate species (cladogenesis) is debated.

articles.title: Centrosaurine diversity
articles.body: The remarkable diversity of centrosaurines — with different genera in different formations, different time slices and different geographic areas — may reflect rapid evolution driven by sexual selection. Different horn and frill configurations served primarily as species recognition billboards rather than weapons; divergence in display structures could drive rapid speciation in socially complex herding animals.

consensusScope: diet, locomotion and major uncertainty wording

record.mya: late Campanian, approximately 75.5-74 million years ago
record.description: Einiosaurus procurvicornis was a centrosaurine ceratopsid from the upper Two Medicine Formation of Montana. Two large bonebeds preserve skull and postcranial material from many individuals and growth stages, documenting a forward-curving nasal horn and a distinctive frill.
facts: The record is a disarticulated multi-individual bonebed, not one complete skeleton.
Nasal horn and frill shape changed during growth.
The bonebeds support group aggregation but do not reveal permanent herd organisation.

review.ageReviewNote: The upper Two Medicine Formation bonebeds are tightly placed in the late Campanian near 75.5-74 Ma.
